title: Diagrams and extensions: naming a structure inside another model
summary: Name every element of a structure to describe its embedded copies, then use compactness to construct proper countable elementary extensions.
abstract: Can we enlarge a structure while keeping every first-order statement about its original elements unchanged? Give each original element a new constant symbol, and collect all the sentences true with those names. Any model of this collection contains a copy of the original structure that agrees with it on every formula with original parameters. In a countable language, compactness then gives every countably infinite structure a proper countable elementary extension. For the natural-number order, a suitable extension even has a point above every original natural number, although it still has no greatest element. The construction also explains why negative atomic facts matter for embeddings and why finite structures admit no proper elementary extensions.
